content.content:
# markdown-s3 — Personal Markdown wiki with live-preview editor (tier S3) Node.js 22, standard library only (no runtime npm dependencies). Single user, no authentication. ## 1. Renderer `src/markdown.js` (ES module) - `export function render(markdown, { headingIds = false, wikiLinks } = {})` → HTML. - `export function toc(markdown)` → `[{ level, text, slug }]`; `export function slugify(text, seen?)`. Rendering rules: CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by commonmark.js) plus GFM pipe tables and `~~strikethrough~~` (``). Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags does not matter; `
`/`
`, `
`/`
`, ``/`` are equivalent; table alignment may be `align="x"` or `style="text-align:x"`. Required: ATX/setext headings, paragraphs, hard breaks, emphasis/strong, code spans, fenced + indented code (`class="language-"`), blockquotes, nested bullet/ordered lists (tight/loose, `start`), inline/reference links, images, autolinks, backslash escapes, tables, thematic breaks. Safety (deviation from CommonMark): raw HTML is rendered as escaped text; link/image URLs with schemes `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`, or `data:` (except `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`) become `#`. Slugs (GitHub style): lower-case, drop every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`, spaces → `-`; with a `Map` `seen`, duplicates get `-1`, `-2`, …. `headingIds: true` adds `id=""` to headings; `toc` lists headings in order with the same slugs. Wiki links (when `wikiLinks` is given as `{ exists(slug) → boolean }`): `[[Page Title]]` → `Page Title`; `[[target|label]]` → link to `slugify(target)` with text `label`. If `exists(slug)` is false the class is `wikilink missing`. Wiki links inside code spans/blocks are not converted. Without the option `[[x]]` is plain text. ## 2. Server `src/server.js` `export function createServer({ dataDir })` → `node:http` Server (not listening). All state is stored under `dataDir` and survives a restart (new server, same directory). JSON bodies; errors `{ "error": "", "message": "" }` with 400 (validation / bad JSON), 404 (unknown page/version/route), 409 (conflict). Pages: `{ slug, title, body, tags[], version, createdAt, updatedAt }`. `slug` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` (else 400). `title` non-empty ≤ 200 chars. Tags are lower-cased, de-duplicated, sorted. - `PUT /api/pages/:slug {title, body, tags?, baseVersion?}` → creates (201, version 1) or updates (200, version+1). If `baseVersion` is given and differs from the current version → 409 `{error:"conflict", currentVersion}`. A PUT whose title, body and tags are unchanged does not create a new version (200, same version). - `GET /api/pages/:slug` → page plus `html` (rendered with `headingIds: true` and wiki links resolved against existing pages), `toc`, `backlinks` (sorted slugs of pages whose current body links to this page via a wiki link), `links` (sorted distinct target slugs of this page's wiki links). - `GET /api/pages?tag=&sort=title|updated` → `[{ slug, title, tags, version, updatedAt }]`; default sort `title` (case-insensitive), `updated` = newest first. - `DELETE /api/pages/:slug` → 204 (history removed too). - History: `GET /api/pages/:slug/history` → `[{ version, title, updatedAt }]` newest first; `GET /api/pages/:slug/versions/:n` → that version's `{ version, title, body, tags }`; `POST /api/pages/:slug/revert {version}` → creates a new version whose content equals that version (200). - Diff: `GET /api/pages/:slug/diff?from=a&to=b` → `{ from, to, lines: [{ op, text }] }`, a minimal line-based diff of the bodies (LCS) with `op` ∈ `" "` (unchanged), `"-"` (only in `from`), `"+"` (only in `to`); inside each changed run all `-` lines come before `+` lines. - Search: `GET /api/search?q=` (case-insensitive, ≥ 1 char after trimming else 400) → `[{ slug, title, snippet, score }]` for pages whose title or body contains `q`. Order: title matches first, then by number of occurrences in title+body (desc), then slug. `snippet`: up to 40 characters before and after the first body occurrence (or the start of the body when only the title matches), HTML-escaped, with the matched text wrapped in `…` (original case). - `POST /api/render {markdown}` → `{ html, toc }` (wiki links resolved against existing pages). - `GET /api/tags` → `[{ tag, count }]` sorted by tag. - `GET /api/export` → `{ pages: [{ slug, title, body, tags, version }] }`; `POST /api/import {pages}` → creates/updates each page (new version if changed) → `{ imported }`. - `GET /wiki/:slug` → a standalone HTML document (`text/html`) containing the page title and the same `html` as `GET /api/pages/:slug` (heading ids, resolved wiki links); 404 page for unknown slugs. ## 3. Editor UI `GET /` serves a single-page app (`text/html`; extra assets under `/static/`) with: page list with tag filter, search box, a Markdown editor with live preview (via `/api/render`), save with conflict handling (`baseVersion`), history view with diff, backlinks panel. The UI must use only the public API. `src/main.js` starts the server on `PORT` (default 3000) with `DATA_DIR` (default `./data`). .: PROVENANCE.json SPEC.md package.json tests ./tests: public ./tests/public: smoke.test.js

content.text:
The wiki is built and `node --test` passes (2 tests: the public smoke test and one I wrote).

My test covers the server only. The renderer got a quick manual check on a few inputs (headings, wiki links, tables, `<del>`, unsafe URLs) but has no tests. I didn't open the editor UI in a browser or run `src/main.js`.

**How I built it:**
- **Renderer (`src/markdown.js`):** I vendored markdown-it 15.0.3 (MIT, unmodified) instead of writing a CommonMark parser. The estimate was that a CommonMark+GFM parser is large and error-prone to write, and the bundle gives tables and strikethrough.
- **Custom rules on top of markdown-it:** I added `<del>` for strikethrough, URL sanitising, heading ids with `toc` and `slugify`, and wiki links (`[[x]]` and `[[target|label]]`, skipped inside code).
- **Spec conformance:** I didn't check the output against commonmark.js, so some edge cases may differ.
- **Server (`src/server.js`):** I wrote this myself. It covers every endpoint in the spec, including the 409 conflict response and the LCS diff. Each page is stored as a JSON file under `dataDir/pages`, so state survives a restart.
- **Editor UI (`src/static/`):** I wrote a small app with the page list, tag filter, search box, live preview, save with conflict handling, history with diff and revert, and backlinks. It uses only the public API.
- **Entry point (`src/main.js`):** It reads `PORT` (default 3000) and `DATA_DIR` (default `./data`).

`PROVENANCE.json` and `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` record the markdown-it vendoring and its license.
